A Message to Our Valued Stockists
Since the first Zamco toaster rolled off the line, one promise has guided everything we do: more product, for more people, more often.
Today Zamco proudly delivers joy to over forty habitation rings. Our family of products includes:
- Aug Warriors, the trading card game. The station's #1 card game!*
- CyberNocts, collectible buildable robot figures. Coming soon!
- Lil' Debtors, plush pals that grow with your outstanding balance.
- Zamco SmartCrib. It watches the baby so you can work a second shift.
Thank you for stocking Zamco. Remember: you're not just selling toys. You're selling the feeling of almost having enough.
Zamco Electronics. Better living through hardware.

The card game the whole station is talking about. Build the ultimate mercenary one augment at a time, then outplay your rivals at the showdown.

Every booster pack is factory sealed at Zamco's orbital plant and holds a random assortment of cards: commons, uncommons and, if fortune smiles, something rare.** Collect them, trade them, grade them, play them.
Booster boxes, Collector's Boxes, binders and deck boxes are available from participating retailers. Collect the whole set!
Authorized dealers: hang your Zamco Dealer Certificate in your display case, and collectors will know where to find you.
**Rarity not guaranteed. Collecting the whole set not guaranteed.
Where to Buy: the Downside Den
Zamco products are sold by fine retailers across the station, and by one that isn't so fine.

Take the service lift down past the recycling decks. Step off where the lights stop working properly, follow the smell of fried noodles and the sound of shuffling, and look for the hand-painted sign: DOWNSIDE DEN.

Ask for Dan. He stocks fresh booster packs and boxes every night, keeps singles in the case, and buys collectibles over the counter. The Den opens after hours: drop by once your own shop has closed for the night.
The back table belongs to the station's Aug Warriors regulars. Bring a deck.
Two mercenaries race to build the strongest body. Each body has five slots: head, torso, two arms and legs.
Every augment you install adds Power, and most add Glitch too. Your Stability starts at 3; torsos and some mods raise it.
At the showdown the higher Power wins. But if your total Glitch is over your Stability, you are Compromised and keep only half your Power.
The art of the game: push your Power as high as you dare without letting the Glitch get away from you.
Both players start with 4 cards, and a coin toss decides who goes first.
At the start of your turn, draw a card if you hold fewer than 4. Then do one thing:
- Play a card: install an augment, attach a mod, or hack your opponent.
- Call the showdown. Your opponent gets one last turn, and draws 2 extra cards for it.
If you have nothing you can play, you must call. On the last turn, if there's nothing to play, the turn simply passes.
The showdown also happens on its own once both players have taken 6 turns. A tie goes to whoever did not call; if nobody called, it's a draw.
AUGMENTS go into the matching slot of your own body; an arm augment fits either arm. Installing over an augment replaces it, and its mods are lost.
MODS attach to one of your installed augments, up to 2 on each. Some only fit certain slots. A good mod soaks up Glitch or adds Stability.
HACKS are played on your opponent's installed augments. Most add Glitch to the target, and it stacks. Scrap hacks remove the augment and its mods entirely.

Some augments do more: draw cards when installed, make you immune to hacks, gain Power for each mod on them, for each of your Glitch-free augments or if you called the showdown, or soften the blow of being Compromised. The numbers are printed on each card.
A torso augment: Power 1, Stability 3, Glitch 0.
The small cards on the Aug Warriors table carry these symbols:
Power. The number in the top corner.
Mod. Attaches to one of your augments.
Hack. Played on your opponent's augments.
Glitch it adds, or removes with a minus. On a hack, the Glitch it adds to the target.
Scrap: removes the target augment and its mods.
A legal deck has 10 to 20 cards, with no more than 2 copies of any one card. Keep it in a deck box: the box's Validate button checks it for you.
- Bring a torso. It's your best source of Stability.
- Pack at least 2 arm augments, a head and legs, so you can fill your body.
- Don't run more mods than augments: mods need something to sit on.
- A few hacks keep greedy opponents honest.
- Watch your Glitch. Half of a big number is often a small number.
Deck builders may also come to your shop with a box and a wish list. Fill it to their order and they'll pay well for the work.
Some nights the Den's regulars are at the back table, up for a game. Who shows up, and how they play, is for you to find out. Fans of the game may also ask for a quick match at your counter.
Put your deck box in the Deck slot, then choose your stakes:
- Credits: the winner takes the pot.
- A card: win and you keep it, plus a new card of the same rarity (sometimes better, often one you don't own yet). Lose and your opponent keeps it.
Or play for nothing at all, just for the glory.
